# Specification Quality Checklist: sing-box TUI

**Purpose**: Validate specification completeness and quality before proceeding to planning
**Created**: 2026-10-05
**Feature**: [spec.md](../spec.md)

**Note**: This custom checklist is generated by the `/speckit.checklist` command based on feature context and requirements.
**Review Ownership**: This checklist is a reviewer-owned requirements-quality review artifact. Mark an item `[x]` only when the reviewer determines the requirements-quality criterion is satisfied.
**Marker Semantics**: `[x]` means the criterion has been reviewed and satisfied for requirements quality. It does not mean implementation work is complete.

## Content Quality

- [x] No implementation details (languages, frameworks, APIs)
- [x] Focused on user value and business needs
- [x] Written for non-technical stakeholders
- [x] All mandatory sections completed

## Requirement Completeness

- [x] No [NEEDS CLARIFICATION] markers remain
- [x] Requirements are testable and unambiguous
- [x] Success criteria are measurable
- [x] Success criteria are technology-agnostic (no implementation details)
- [x] All acceptance scenarios are defined
- [x] Edge cases are identified
- [x] Scope is clearly bounded
- [x] Dependencies and assumptions identified

## Feature Readiness

- [x] All functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria
- [x] User scenarios cover primary flows
- [x] Feature meets measurable outcomes defined in Success Criteria
- [x] No implementation details leak into specification

## Validation Findings

Reviewed 2026-10-05 against the written spec.

**Passing items**

- *No implementation details*: Requirements describe behaviour and observable outcomes only. No language, framework, library, or API is named. The only environment references (macOS, sing-box 1.14.x, the config path, elevated privileges) are user-stated facts recorded in **Assumptions**, not implementation choices.
- *Mandatory sections*: User Scenarios & Testing, Requirements, and Success Criteria are all present and populated. Key Entities is included because the feature presents structured configuration data.
- *Testable requirements*: Each FR names an observable behaviour with a pass/fail condition (for example FR-011 requires three distinct failure reasons to be distinguished; FR-022 requires survival of terminal resize).
- *Measurable, technology-agnostic success criteria*: SC-001 to SC-015 use time, count, and percentage measures expressed from the user's viewpoint ("within 3 seconds of launching", "10 consecutive launches", "at most three scrolls of that panel"). No framework, tool, or internal metric appears.
- *Acceptance scenarios*: Four prioritised stories, each independently testable, with 33 Given/When/Then scenarios (8, 10, 6, 8) covering running, stopped, degraded, failure, unprivileged, and exit states.
- *Edge cases*: 18 cases covering missing binary, invalid config, warnings-only config, multiple config files, running-but-degraded tunnel, no traffic flowing, unprivileged execution, interrupted tests, unresolvable/blocked targets, unreachable address reference, small and resized terminals with four panels, no-color/SSH output, internationalised domain rendering, long rule lists, quit during a pending action, a stop that fails, and a service owned by another account.
- *Scope bounded*: FR-026 (must not modify the config) and the Assumptions section explicitly place config editing and alternate config profiles out of scope.
- *Dependencies and assumptions*: The existing sing-box install, the config path, the privilege requirement, and the absence of the optional management API are all recorded as assumptions.

**Failing items**

- None. The single failing item from the first pass has been resolved.

**Resolution log**

- *Iteration 1* (2026-10-05): one `[NEEDS CLARIFICATION]` marker at FR-019 on process-control scope. Presented to the user together with two secondary scope questions whose defaults were documented rather than marked. All three were answered with the recommended option, and the spec was updated:
  - Process control: **full control** — FR-019 de-marked; FR-019a (externally started instance requires explicit confirmation before stop), FR-019b (exit states what is left running), FR-020a (declined/timed-out privilege prompt is "action not performed") added; User Story 4 scenario 5 rewritten; three new edge cases added; SC-011 and SC-012 added.
  - Ping: **default target set plus user-entered targets**, on demand and cancellable — already covered by FR-008 to FR-012; confirmed in the new Confirmed Decisions section.
  - Config: **read-only plus validation** — already covered by FR-013 to FR-017 and FR-026; editing and profile switching recorded as out of scope.
- *Iteration 2* (2026-10-05): re-reviewed the full spec against every item on this checklist. All items pass.

**Clarification pass** (2026-10-05, `/speckit.clarify`)

Five questions asked and answered; all five integrated. Checkbox states unchanged: **16/16 passing before, 16/16 passing after** — no newly checked items and no regressions.

- **Privilege model** → launch-time elevation, no in-app password. Removed the now-invalid password-prompt requirement and its two edge cases; added FR-020a (detect missing elevation), FR-020b (resolve the config path against the invoking user's home), SC-013, SC-014, and rewrote Story 4 scenarios 1 and 2.
- **Quit behaviour** → quitting always stops the service. Replaced the ambiguous "must not leave the service in an unexpected state" edge case with explicit stop-on-quit and stop-failure cases; rewrote FR-019b and Story 4 scenarios 7 and 8; added SC-012a.
- **Status state model** → four lifecycle states plus a separate three-value health badge. FR-002 and FR-007 rewritten, FR-002a added for stuck transitions, Key Entities updated, Story 1 scenario 3a added and renumbered to 4, SC-009a added.
- **Layout** → single dashboard with four focusable panels, no tabs. FR-013 rewritten with FR-013a added, FR-018/FR-021/FR-022 updated, SC-003 and SC-005 restated in panel terms, and the vocabulary normalised throughout ("options view", "ping view", "log view", "route taken" all removed).
- **Route attribution** → both inferred and measured. FR-010 split into FR-010 (inferred, no outside dependency) and FR-010a (measured address, on demand), FR-011 extended with "reference unavailable", new Observed Address entity, new Story 2 scenario and edge case, SC-015 added, and the outside-reference dependency recorded in Assumptions.

**Gaps closed during this pass** (so "all functional requirements have clear acceptance criteria" remains genuinely true rather than by omission): three acceptance scenarios were added for requirements that had none — Story 1 scenario 8 for FR-002a (stuck transition), Story 1 scenario 9 for FR-013/FR-021/FR-022 and SC-005 (four panels and focus at 80x24 without color), and Story 3 scenario 6 for FR-020b and FR-025 (config path resolved against the invoking user's home).

## Notes

- Items marked incomplete require spec updates before `/speckit.clarify` or `/speckit.plan`
- The project constitution at `.specify/memory/constitution.md` is still the unedited Spec Kit template (placeholders such as `[PRINCIPLE_1_NAME]`), so no project-specific governance constraints were applied during this validation. Consider ratifying a constitution before `/speckit.plan`.
- The user's live config emits a deprecation warning (`independent_cache`) from the config checker; FR-017 covers surfacing such warnings verbatim.
